english.title: Sponsor fail to inform investigator of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions in a clinical trial

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Medicines for human Use Clinical Trials Regulations 2004

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the sponsor of a clinical trial in the United Kingdom, failed to ensure that the investigators responsible for the conduct of the trial were informed of a suspected unexpected serious adverse reaction which occurred in relation to an investigational medicinal product used in that trial
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 33(5), 49(1)(h) and 52 of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

sponsor did not ensure

which occurred in relation to

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: (i) Regulation 51 of the of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 provides a defence of due diligence.(ii) This offence should not be used after 27th April 2026 as it has been revoked by the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) (Amendment) Regulations 2025.
